about: Stages and timing for the autosuggest-cleanup playbook. scripts/handoff.py reads this file: the stages it tracks, the outcomes each stage can record, and how long to wait between stages. Each key is explained under notes.

stages.name: audit
stages.do: Audit what autosuggest offers for the top queries' prefixes, add the suggestions to hide and the exclusions to undo as findings, and agree which to act on.

stages.name: exclude
stages.do: Plan the agreed exclusions with a before and after preview, create new rules disabled and switch them on, each batch after its own yes, staging first.

skip_when.reason: the audit found no suggestion worth hiding or bringing back.

stages.name: recheck
stages.do: Audit autosuggest again: check the excluded suggestions stay gone, what shoppers are offered instead, and anything new to fix.

skip_when.reason: no exclusion went live, so there is nothing to re-check.
the exclude stage was skipped, so nothing changed.

notes.recheck_after_days: Days after the exclude stage finishes (the exclusions went live) before the recheck stage is due. Suggestions disappear within minutes of a rule syncing, which the exclusions skill already verifies; the recheck looks at what shoppers search instead, and autosuggest-audit reads 30 days of query performance by default, so four whole weeks gives it a window that starts after the change, with the same weekday mix.
notes.max_chosen: How many findings can be chosen at once. The exclude stage acts on every exclusion the user agrees in one plan, up to this many.
notes.playbooks: Each playbook's title, product and stages in order. A stage names the skill that does it, whether that skill writes, what to do, the outcomes it can record, not_before (wait this rules key's number of days after another stage is done) and skip_when (suggest skipping when an earlier stage had one of these outcomes, or with skipped: true when it was skipped). The same skill may run twice: the recheck stage repeats the audit.
